qs.q: A patient with primary hyperparathyroidism is scheduled for preoperative imaging. Why is technetium-99m sestamibi scintigraphy particularly effective for localising parathyroid adenomas?
o: The adenoma retains the radiotracer due to oxyphil mitochondria
The radiotracer is selectively absorbed by chief cell nuclear DNA
The tracer binds directly to extracellular calcium-sensing receptors
Increased blood flow washes out the tracer from normal tissue slowly
qs.e: Parathyroid adenomas retain technetium-99m sestamibi due to the abundance of mitochondria in their oxyphil cells. This allows for scintigraphic differentiation from normal surrounding thyroid or lymph node tissue.

qs.q: A 50‑year‑old man with MEN 1 has a single parathyroid adenoma confirmed by concordant imaging. Which surgical approach is most appropriate?
qs.e: A single adenoma in MEN 1 is best treated with a focused, minimally invasive procedure guided by imaging.
qs.s: Hyperparathyroidism: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary and Parathyroid: MCQs

qs.q: A patient develops perioral tingling and carpopedal spasm immediately after removal of a large parathyroid adenoma. Which complication is most likely?
qs.e: Rapid bone remineralisation after removal of a suppressed gland causes hungry bone syndrome, presenting with hypocalcaemia and tetany.
qs.s: Hyperparathyroidism: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary and Parathyroid: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old man is found to have a hyperfunctioning parathyroid adenoma located within the anterior mediastinum. Which approach provides the optimal minimally invasive access for resection?
qs.e: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery allows direct visualization and removal of anterior mediastinal ectopic glands. Sternotomy is rarely needed unless the lesion is deeply embedded.

qs.q: What histological finding helps distinguish a parathyroid adenoma from parathyroid hyperplasia?
o: Invasion of surrounding thyroid capsule and blood vessels
Involvement and enlargement of all four glands equally
Abundant clear glycogen-rich cytoplasm in all cells
A rim of compressed normal parathyroid tissue at the edge
qs.e: The presence of a compressed rim of normal parathyroid tissue at the periphery is a hallmark of a solitary adenoma. In contrast, hyperplasia typically affects all four glands without a normal rim.

qs.q: Which finding is characteristic of parathyroid adenomas in terms of their cellular composition?
o: Mostly composed of chief cells with rare oxyphil adenomas
qs.e: Parathyroid adenomas are mostly composed of chief cells, while oxyphil adenomas are rare. Chief cells serve as the primary functional cell type in the gland.
